allVulnerabilities.name: BDSA-2026-3348
allVulnerabilities.description: Underscore.js is vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) due to unbounded recursion in the `_.flatten` and `_.isEqual` functions. Both functions recursively traverse nested data structures without enforcing a depth limit, making them susceptible to stack overflow errors when processing deeply nested input. This could allow an attacker to craft a malicious payload, such as a JSON object or array nested approximately 4,500 levels deep, and submit it to an application that passes untrusted input to either function, causing the application to crash.
allVulnerabilities.solution:
Fixed in [**1.13.8**](https://github.com/jashkenas/underscore/releases/tag/1.13.8) by [this](https://github.com/jashkenas/underscore/commit/411e222eb0ca5d570cc4f6315c02c05b830ed2b4) commit and [this](https://github.com/jashkenas/underscore/commit/a6e23ae9647461ec33ad9f92a2ecfc220eea0a84) commit.

The latest stable releases are available here.
allVulnerabilities.workaround:
The vendor proposes the following workaround:
> A workaround that works for both functions is to enforce a depth limit on the datastructure that is created from untrusted input. A limit of 1000 levels should prevent attacks from being successful on most systems. In systems with highly constrained hardware, we recommend lower limits, for example 100 levels.
> 
> Another possible workaround that only works for `_.flatten`, is to pass a second argument that limits the flattening depth to 1000 or less.

allVulnerabilities.name: BDSA-2019-2162
allVulnerabilities.description: Mixin-deep is vulnerable to prototype pollution attack. This could allow an attacker to manipulate a function to add or modify properties of `Object.prototype` via a constructor payload. Successfully exploiting results in a denial-of-service (DoS) and code execution may be possible.
allVulnerabilities.solution:
Fixed in:

* **[1.3.2](https://github.com/jonschlinkert/mixin-deep/releases/tag/1.3.2)** by [this](https://github.com/jonschlinkert/mixin-deep/commit/90ee1fab375fccfd9b926df718243339b4976d50) commit.

allVulnerabilities.workaround:
1. Freeze the prototype— use Object.freeze (Object.prototype).
2. Require schema validation of JSON input.
3. Avoid using unsafe recursive merge functions.
4. Consider using objects without prototypes (for example, Object.create(null)), breaking the prototype chain and preventing pollution.
5. As a best practice use Map instead of Object.

allVulnerabilities.description: minimatch is a minimal matching utility for converting glob expressions into JavaScript RegExp objects. Prior to version 10.2.3, 9.0.7, 8.0.6, 7.4.8, 6.2.2, 5.1.8, 4.2.5, and 3.1.4, nested `*()` extglobs produce regexps with nested unbounded quantifiers (e.g. `(?:(?:a|b)*)*`), which exhibit catastrophic backtracking in V8. The same issue affects `+()` extglobs equally. Versions 10.2.3, 9.0.7, 8.0.6, 7.4.8, 6.2.2, 5.1.8, 4.2.5, and 3.1.4 fix the issue.

policyViolationVulnerabilities.name: BDSA-2026-2976
policyViolationVulnerabilities.description:
minimatch is vulnerable to a regular expression denial-of-service (ReDoS) issue due to how the `matchOne()` method can perform unbounded recursive backtracking when a glob pattern contains multiple non-adjacent `**` (GLOBSTAR) segments, and the input path does not match.

An attacker could submit a crafted pattern to an affected application in order to cause excessive backtracking conditions that result in processing stalls. The time complexity of the `matchOne` operations is binomial where larger inputs cause excessive stalls.

**Note**: It was [reported](https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/issues/284) that the original fixes for this issue introduced a regression that caused `minimatch` to return incorrect results. The regression corrections have been considered in the **Solution**.

policyViolationVulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-27904
policyViolationVulnerabilities.description: minimatch is a minimal matching utility for converting glob expressions into JavaScript RegExp objects. Prior to version 10.2.3, 9.0.7, 8.0.6, 7.4.8, 6.2.2, 5.1.8, 4.2.5, and 3.1.4, nested `*()` extglobs produce regexps with nested unbounded quantifiers (e.g. `(?:(?:a|b)*)*`), which exhibit catastrophic backtracking in V8. With a 12-byte pattern `*(*(*(a|b)))` and an 18-byte non-matching input, `minimatch()` stalls for over 7 seconds. Adding a single nesting level or a few input characters pushes this to minutes. This is the most severe finding: it is triggered by the default `minimatch()` API with no special options, and the minimum viable pattern is only 12 bytes. The same issue affects `+()` extglobs equally. Versions 10.2.3, 9.0.7, 8.0.6, 7.4.8, 6.2.2, 5.1.8, 4.2.5, and 3.1.4 fix the issue.

It was demonstrated by a security researcher that the bucket became available to register once again, and it was taken over by the researcher to demonstrate possible impact of this vulnerability. At this time, AWS has taken possession of the S3 bucket and currently blocks all access, neutralizing any threat. Should this bucket become available to use in the future, affected versions of fsevents will once again become vulnerable. This occurred in August 2023, when the bucket was briefly reinstated in error.

allVulnerabilities.solution:
Fixed in:
* [**2.5.6**](https://github.com/form-data/form-data/releases/tag/v2.5.6) by [this](https://github.com/form-data/form-data/commit/b62031603c2d7c329b2a369b49466790f0ba6314) commit,

> 
> `if (/[\r\n]/.test(field)) { throw new Error('invalid field name'); }`

allVulnerabilities.description: Underscore.js is vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) due to unbounded recursion in the `_.flatten` and `_.isEqual` functions. Both functions recursively traverse nested data structures without enforcing a depth limit, making them susceptible to stack overflow errors when processing deeply nested input. This could allow an attacker to craft a malicious payload, such as a JSON object or array nested approximately 4,500 levels deep, and submit it to an application that passes untrusted input to either function, causing the application to crash.
allVulnerabilities.solution:
Fixed in [**1.13.8**](https://github.com/jashkenas/underscore/releases/tag/1.13.8) by [this](https://github.com/jashkenas/underscore/commit/411e222eb0ca5d570cc4f6315c02c05b830ed2b4) commit and [this](https://github.com/jashkenas/underscore/commit/a6e23ae9647461ec33ad9f92a2ecfc220eea0a84) commit.

allVulnerabilities.workaround:
The vendor proposes the following workaround:
> A workaround that works for both functions is to enforce a depth limit on the datastructure that is created from untrusted input. A limit of 1000 levels should prevent attacks from being successful on most systems. In systems with highly constrained hardware, we recommend lower limits, for example 100 levels.
> 
> Another possible workaround that only works for `_.flatten`, is to pass a second argument that limits the flattening depth to 1000 or less.

allVulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-27904
allVulnerabilities.description: minimatch is a minimal matching utility for converting glob expressions into JavaScript RegExp objects. Prior to version 10.2.3, 9.0.7, 8.0.6, 7.4.8, 6.2.2, 5.1.8, 4.2.5, and 3.1.4, nested `*()` extglobs produce regexps with nested unbounded quantifiers (e.g. `(?:(?:a|b)*)*`), which exhibit catastrophic backtracking in V8. With a 12-byte pattern `*(*(*(a|b)))` and an 18-byte non-matching input, `minimatch()` stalls for over 7 seconds. Adding a single nesting level or a few input characters pushes this to minutes. This is the most severe finding: it is triggered by the default `minimatch()` API with no special options, and the minimum viable pattern is only 12 bytes. The same issue affects `+()` extglobs equally. Versions 10.2.3, 9.0.7, 8.0.6, 7.4.8, 6.2.2, 5.1.8, 4.2.5, and 3.1.4 fix the issue.

allVulnerabilities.name: BDSA-2026-2976
allVulnerabilities.description:
minimatch is vulnerable to a regular expression denial-of-service (ReDoS) issue due to how the `matchOne()` method can perform unbounded recursive backtracking when a glob pattern contains multiple non-adjacent `**` (GLOBSTAR) segments, and the input path does not match.

An attacker could submit a crafted pattern to an affected application in order to cause excessive backtracking conditions that result in processing stalls. The time complexity of the `matchOne` operations is binomial where larger inputs cause excessive stalls.

**Note**: It was [reported](https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/issues/284) that the original fixes for this issue introduced a regression that caused `minimatch` to return incorrect results. The regression corrections have been considered in the **Solution**.

policyViolationVulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-27904
policyViolationVulnerabilities.description: minimatch is a minimal matching utility for converting glob expressions into JavaScript RegExp objects. Prior to version 10.2.3, 9.0.7, 8.0.6, 7.4.8, 6.2.2, 5.1.8, 4.2.5, and 3.1.4, nested `*()` extglobs produce regexps with nested unbounded quantifiers (e.g. `(?:(?:a|b)*)*`), which exhibit catastrophic backtracking in V8. With a 12-byte pattern `*(*(*(a|b)))` and an 18-byte non-matching input, `minimatch()` stalls for over 7 seconds. Adding a single nesting level or a few input characters pushes this to minutes. This is the most severe finding: it is triggered by the default `minimatch()` API with no special options, and the minimum viable pattern is only 12 bytes. The same issue affects `+()` extglobs equally. Versions 10.2.3, 9.0.7, 8.0.6, 7.4.8, 6.2.2, 5.1.8, 4.2.5, and 3.1.4 fix the issue.

allVulnerabilities.description: form-data is vulnerable to carriage-return/line-feed (CRLF) injection due to improper character escaping. allVulnerabilities.solution:
Fixed in:
* [**2.5.6**](https://github.com/form-data/form-data/releases/tag/v2.5.6) by [this](https://github.com/form-data/form-data/commit/b62031603c2d7c329b2a369b49466790f0ba6314) commit,

allVulnerabilities.workaround:

> Until upgrading, validate or reject field names/filenames that contain control characters before calling append:
> 
> `if (/[\r\n]/.test(field)) { throw new Error('invalid field name'); }`
